editorial.headline: Residential Leasing: Open Nationally, Closed to PMA Registration in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 68112 covers leasing and operating self-owned or rented residential real estate—open to foreign investment nationally, but unavailable for PMA registration at a Bali address.
editorial.body:
KBLI 68112 is the business of leasing and operating residential real estate that the operator owns or itself rents. In practical terms, its focus is the ongoing provision and operation of homes and residential property through a rental model. The wording matters: the scope joins two linked functions—leasing and operating—and applies whether the residential real estate is self-owned or rented by the business. That is the full activity described in the record, and it is the right boundary for deciding whether the code fits a proposed venture.

The record opens the activity to Micro, Small, Medium and Large enterprises. It does not reserve the scope for a single business size. At national level, it is marked open to foreign investment, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. That is a clear national position: a PMA structure may hold up to the stated ceiling for this activity. The source recorded for that national treatment is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Those facts make the national rule unusually straightforward, provided the business remains within residential leasing and operation as stated.

Bali changes the registration answer completely. A foreign investor cannot register this activity through a PMA company at a Bali address today. Although the activity is open at all four enterprise scales, the record identifies its Large scale as Medium-Low for the Bali determination. It is therefore blocked by Bali’s PMA moratorium, which the record says applies island-wide and permanently. The stated reason is not a change to the national foreign-ownership ceiling; it is the Bali rule that blocks this activity’s PMA registration on the island.

The restriction is tied in the record to Governor’s letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP, and its supporting explanation cites a government letter dated May 13, 2026. The practical reading is deliberately narrow but decisive: national openness does not make Bali registration available where the local moratorium blocks it. For a founder considering this exact residential real-estate activity, Indonesia’s national framework and a Bali address produce different outcomes. The national ceiling remains 100%; the Bali PMA route is closed under the recorded moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness does not make Bali registration available where the local moratorium blocks it.
